item.title: CPU-Only Benchmark
item.description:
What Joulie’s policies do to energy per unit of work on a 40-node CPU cluster (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).

Full report: experiments/01-cpu-only-benchmark/REPORT.md.

Setup

Nodes Count CPU Cores Eco cap
kwok-cpu-highcore 10 2 x AMD EPYC 9965 384 600 W
kwok-cpu-highfreq 10 2 x AMD EPYC 9375F 64 384 W
kwok-cpu-intensive 20 2 x AMD EPYC 9655 192 480 W
Item Value
Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (19 of 40 nodes performance); C: queue-aware
Power models SPECpower curves (9655, 9965); analytic model at sockets x TDP (9375F)
Eco cap 60 % of sockets x TDP
Load CPU utilization 0.55 to 0.58 under A
Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime

Results

Baseline Energy per CPU unit against A, seed 1 / 2 Avg IT power against A CPU work done against A
B (static) +2.7 / +1.4 % +2.7 / +1.4 % +0.0 / -0.0 %
C (queue-aware) +2.1 / +2.5 % +1.8 / +2.5 % -0.3 / -0.0 %

A’s repeat differed by 0.24 % in energy per unit.

item.title: Governor Exploration
item.description:
Experiment 05 measures CPU and GPU governor presets as an energy dimension of their own, next to power caps, to choose the defaults Joulie ships. The results come from emulated nodes whose governor and clock physics rest on assumed parameters: they show the shape of each trade-off, not measured savings (#106).

Experiment folder: experiments/05-governor-exploration/. The presets are under Governor presets; governor control is off by default (GOVERNOR_CONTROL, GOVERNOR_WRITES, Configuration reference).

Questions

  • Q1: per CPU driver, which preset minimises energy to solution at each load, and at what cost in time?
  • Q2: per GPU family and workload kind, energy and time of each GPU preset, alone and with a 60 % cap?
  • Q3: with a receiver gate, how much do multi-GPU jobs gain from sustained?
  • Q4: at cluster level, do governors beat caps alone on energy without breaking the performance class?
  • Q5: which conclusions survive the assumed parameters?

A default passes on a profile when it lowers energy with a p95 slowdown of at most 5 % (performance class) and 20 % (eco class), in Tier A, in Tier B and at every value Q5 sweeps.

item.title: Heterogeneous GPU Cluster Benchmark
item.description:
What Joulie’s policies do to energy per unit of GPU work on a 41-node cluster of five GPU families (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).

Full report: experiments/02-heterogeneous-benchmark/REPORT.md.

Setup

Nodes Count GPUs per node
kwok-h100-nvl 12 8 x NVIDIA H100 NVL
kwok-h100-sxm 6 4 x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
kwok-l40s 7 4 x NVIDIA L40S
kwok-mi300x 2 8 x AMD Instinct MI300X
kwok-w7900 6 4 x AMD Radeon PRO W7900
CPU-only (EPYC 9965, 9375F, 9655) 8 none
Item Value
Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (31 of 41 nodes performance); C: queue-aware
Eco cap 70 % of each GPU’s maximum
Cap response exponent fitted per family to published data: H100 SXM 0.43, H100 NVL 0.50, MI300X 0.62, L40S 1.20, W7900 1.0 (no data)
Load GPU utilization 0.46 to 0.49 under A
Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime

Results

Baseline GPU-node energy per GPU unit against A, seed 1 / 2 Avg IT power against A GPU work done against A Pending performance jobs (A: 0.7)
B (static) +0.1 / +4.6 % +3.6 / +3.0 % +3.6 / -1.4 % 3.5
C (queue-aware) +1.2 / +2.9 % -1.0 / +0.8 % -2.3 / -2.1 % 5.8

A’s repeat differed by 0.56 % in energy per unit.

item.title: Homogeneous H100 NVL Benchmark
item.description:
What Joulie’s policies do to power and energy per unit of GPU work on a 41-node cluster of H100 NVL nodes (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).

Full report: experiments/03-homogeneous-h100-benchmark/REPORT.md.

Setup

Item Value
Nodes 33 H100 NVL nodes (8 GPUs each) and 8 CPU-only nodes
Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (27 of 41 nodes performance); C: queue-aware
Eco cap 280 W, 70 % of 400 W
Cap response computeGamma 0.50, the H100 PCIe’s published response, since the NVL has no published data (#106)
Load GPU utilization 0.55 to 0.58 under A
Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime

Results

Baseline GPU-node energy per GPU unit against A, seed 1 / 2 Avg IT power against A GPU work done against A Pending performance jobs (A: 0.7)
B (static) +0.5 / -0.2 % -5.7 / -7.1 % -6.5 / -7.5 % 9.2
C (queue-aware) +0.3 / +0.7 % -5.8 / -8.8 % -6.4 / -10.0 % 9.8

A’s repeat differed by 0.01 % in energy per unit. B and C were not repeated, so their own noise is unknown (#113).

item.title: Scoring Formula Validation
item.description:
Not a valid result. Its results do not stand and are not published. The experiment is to be redone on the scheduling logic extracted into an importable library (#122), as a behaviour scenario (#115).

An audit found that jobs that do not fit are dropped instead of queued, energy is divided by the placed jobs only, the arms are mislabelled, the selected formula never ran through the cooling model, and the formula was chosen and reported on the same 8 seeds. The scripts are Python models of the cluster, the cooling and the formula; they import no Joulie code and do not follow changes to the extender.
